items.markdown:
[Jobs to be Done (JTBD)](https://www.christenseninstitute.org/theory/jobs-to-be-done/) is `a business framework stating that people do not simply buy products or services; they "hire" them to make progress and solve specific problems in their lives`.[[1]](https://www.christenseninstitute.org/theory/jobs-to-be-done/)

Pioneered by [Tony Ulwick](https://strategyn.com/) and later popularized by Harvard Business School professor [Clayton Christensen](https://online.hbs.edu/blog/post/jobs-to-be-done-examples) , the theory shifts focus away from traditional demographics and product attributes toward the underlying motivations behind consumer choices.[[1]](https://strategyn.com/jobs-to-be-done/)[[2]](https://www.christenseninstitute.org/theory/jobs-to-be-done/)


---

### Core Principles of JTBD

- **The "Hire" Analogy:** Just as you hire a contractor to build a house, you "hire" a product to perform a specific task when a need arises. If the product fails at the task, you "fire" it and switch to a competitor.[[1]](https://www.christenseninstitute.org/theory/jobs-to-be-done/)[[2]](https://productschool.com/resources/glossary/jobs-to-be-done)
- **Jobs Are Stable:** While products, technologies, and competitors change constantly, the core "job" a customer is trying to accomplish remains remarkably stable over time.[[1]](https://strategyn.com/jobs-to-be-done/)
- **Three Dimensions:** A complete job includes **functional** tasks, alongside the **social** and **emotional** dimensions of how a user wants to feel or be perceived while doing it.[[1]](https://www.christenseninstitute.org/theory/jobs-to-be-done/)[[2]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/jobs-to-be-done-jtbd-framework)


---

### The JTBD Formula
To define a customer job, researchers and product teams often use a context-driven statement structure:[[1]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/jobs-to-be-done-jtbd-framework)> *"When [Circumstance], I want to [Job/Task], so I can [Expected Outcome] without [Pain Point]."* [[1]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/jobs-to-be-done-jtbd-framework)


---

### Real-World Examples

- **The Milkshake Marketing:** A fast-food restaurant found that morning commuters bought milkshakes and nothing else. They weren't looking for a sweet dessert; they "hired" the thick milkshake to keep them full and stave off boredom during a long, monotonous drive.[[1]](https://online.hbs.edu/blog/post/jobs-to-be-done-examples)
- **Snickers vs. Kit Kat:** While both are chocolate candy bars, Snickers targets the functional job of satisfying intense hunger as a meal replacement, whereas Kit Kat targets the emotional job of taking a relaxing mid-day break.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KPeaxDfBnFs)
- **Spotify:** Users don't just "hire" Spotify to stream media files; they hire it to easily control their mood and soundtrack the mundane or important moments of their daily lives.[[1]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/jobs-to-be-done-jtbd-framework)
